elements.title: Grammar Spotlight: Present Perfect Continuous vs Past Simple (B1)
elements.content:
Use the Present Perfect Continuous (have/has been + verb-ing) to describe ongoing activities, research, or habits that started in the past and continue into the present.
Use the Past Simple (verb-ed / irregular) for completed actions at a definite time in the past.

elements.content: Examine common linguistic pitfalls and refine your accuracy with teacher guidance:

pairs.incorrect: Scientists are tracking the kids since eight years.
pairs.correct: Scientists have been tracking the kids for eight years.
pairs.note: Use Present Perfect Continuous with 'for' to describe continuous duration up to now.

pairs.incorrect: Too much screen time make children tired.
pairs.correct: Too much screen time makes children tired.
pairs.note: Uncountable noun phrase 'too much screen time' requires a singular verb.
